# Public Health & Respiratory Exposure Brief — New Delhi, India

*Generated 2026-11-20 14:51 UTC · Profile: **Asthma / Respiratory** · Source: Open-Meteo Air Quality*

**Location:** 28.621, 77.215 · elevation 211 m · Asia/Kolkata

## Current Conditions
- **US AQI:** 211 (Very Unhealthy) · European AQI 105
- **PM2.5:** 151.3 µg/m³ · **PM10:** 151.8 µg/m³ · **NO2:** 109.0 µg/m³ · **O3:** 42.0 µg/m³ · **CO:** 4593 µg/m³
- **Dominant driver:** PM2.5 Fine Particulates (10.09× WHO guideline)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Next 24h | 228.4 | 238 | 156.9 | 157.9 | 89.4 |
| Next 48h | 228.3 | 238 | 153.1 | 154.1 | 81.6 |
| Next 72h | 227.3 | 238 | 147.1 | 148.1 | 77.7 |

- **Trend:** Stable
- **Best outdoor window (next 24h):** Fri 19:00 – Fri 22:00 (mean AQI 211.3)
- **Peak exposure hazard window:** Sat 07:00 – Sat 10:00 (mean AQI 237.3)

## Advisory — Asthma / Respiratory
**Very Unhealthy air for Asthma / Respiratory — dominated by PM2.5 Fine Particulates**

- **Outdoor activity:** Avoid prolonged outdoor activity; stay indoors with filtered air. Best window: Fri 19:00 – Fri 22:00.
- **Mask protocol:** Wear a fitted N95/FFP2 respirator outdoors when US AQI exceeds 100. Mask recommended now. (N95/FFP2 at US AQI > 100)
- **Indoor HEPA filtration:** Run a HEPA purifier sized to the room; keep windows closed during peak hours.
- **Exercise guidance:** Exercise indoors only until AQI falls below 100.

**Symptom watch:**
- Coughing or wheeze
- Chest tightness or shortness of breath
- Eye/throat irritation
- Unusual fatigue or palpitations
